name: Swarm SQLite task store

findings.title: COMMIT failure leaves an open transaction on the process-wide shared connection
findings.summary: create_task drives a raw BEGIN/COMMIT; the success arm propagates a COMMIT error with `?` and never ROLLBACKs. The connection is a single boot-time Arc<Mutex<Connection>> shared with SqliteSnapshotStore, so a dangling transaction permanently poisons every later write on that connection.
findings.failure_scenario: COMMIT returns SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_FULL/IO error -> create_task returns Err with the transaction still open -> every subsequent create_task fails at BEGIN with 'cannot start a transaction within a transaction' and all other writes (snapshots, update_task, run rows, comments) join the never-committed transaction for the life of the process.
findings.fix: Use conn.unchecked_transaction() (RAII, rolls back on Drop) instead of literal BEGIN/COMMIT; or at minimum ROLLBACK explicitly on the COMMIT error path.

findings.title: metadata is a whole-blob overwrite with no CAS; concurrent stampers lose updates silently
findings.summary: update_task replaces the whole metadata column with no version guard, while nine read-modify-write producers across the dispatcher tick, model tools, and panel RPC stamp markers into it concurrently.
findings.failure_scenario: reclaim.rs:285 stamps stale_review_warned_at from a tick snapshot while gateway/handlers/teams/workflow.rs:640 stamps an approval marker from its own snapshot; last writer wins the whole blob. Lost workflow_notified re-fires 'Team work complete'; lost PAUSED_FROM_KEY makes resume re-execute instead of restoring the review gate. No error, no log.
findings.fix: Add an expected-revision guard to CoordTaskUpdate, or expose update_task_metadata_patch(id, patch) implemented with json_patch inside the connection mutex.

findings.title: No index on coord_task_dependencies(depends_on)
findings.summary: The only index is the PRIMARY KEY (task_id, depends_on) autoindex, which cannot serve depends_on-keyed lookups by the leftmost-prefix rule.
findings.failure_scenario: get_dependents (deps.rs:25) and get_newly_unblocked's join (deps.rs:48, runs on every task completion) full-scan the edge table; the ON DELETE CASCADE child scan makes delete_team_tasks O(deleted_tasks x total_edges).
findings.fix: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_coord_task_deps_depends_on ON coord_task_dependencies(depends_on);

findings.title: The create-time cycle check is structurally vacuous and costs an O(V+E) BFS per create
findings.summary: check_no_cycle_sync searches the ancestors of blocked_by for an id minted by Uuid::new_v4() three lines earlier, so no edge can reference it and the guard can never return Err. Redline R10 / CLAUDE.md section 0: an always-true predicate is not a check.
findings.failure_scenario: workflow::compile materialises an n-step chain: each create runs a full ancestor BFS issuing one query per visited node with the global DB mutex held, i.e. O(n^2) edge queries, for a branch that is unreachable by construction. A future add-dependency-to-existing-task path would look protected while it is not.
findings.fix: Drop the call from create_task and document the real invariant (edges only inserted at creation, node has no dependents => acyclic by construction); keep check_no_cycle_sync for the first path that mutates edges on an existing task.

findings.title: list_tasks is unbounded: no LIMIT, no cursor, no row cap
findings.summary: CoordTaskFilter carries only status and team_id; every matching row is materialised with full description/result/metadata JSON plus a GROUP_CONCAT of dependency ids, decoded while holding the global connection mutex.
findings.failure_scenario: A long-lived team's coord_tasks table only grows (no pruning except explicit team deletion); the mutex is held for the whole decode, blocking the dispatcher tick. Callers needing only ids (gateway/handlers/teams/crud.rs:189) pay full price, and snapshots/operations.rs:83 embeds the whole result in a snapshot payload.
findings.fix: Add limit + keyset cursor (created_before) to CoordTaskFilter, applying the derived-status post-filter inside the paging loop; add a list_task_ids(team_id) for id-only callers.

findings.title: metadata serialization failure is silently swallowed on create but errors on update
findings.summary: create_task uses unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}") while update_task:148 returns an error for the identical operation.
findings.failure_scenario: A metadata value that fails to serialize is replaced with an empty object and the task is created as if nothing happened - no error, not even a warn!.
findings.fix: Mirror update_task: map_err(|e| db_err(format!("failed to serialize metadata: {e}")))?

findings.title: row.get(N).ok() conflates NULL, type error, and missing column
findings.summary: The three Phase-C review columns are read with .ok(), which maps a genuine decode failure and a NULL to the same None; from_stored then silently drops unrecognised verdict/kind strings.
findings.failure_scenario: A review_verdict written by a newer build reads back as 'never reviewed' on the audit trail whose purpose is recording who approved what - with no warning. Contrast read_task_row, which raises FromSqlConversionFailure for the same class of corruption.
findings.fix: Use row.get::<_, Option<String>>(8)? for nullability and tracing::warn! when from_stored rejects a non-NULL value.

findings.title: Run ordering relies on second-granularity started_at; ties resolved only by SQLite scan order
findings.summary: record_run_review picks ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1 and list_task_runs returns ORDER BY started_at ASC, but now_epoch() is whole seconds.
findings.failure_scenario: The busy-deferral path files an Abandoned row and immediately re-dispatches, producing two runs in the same second. The tie currently resolves by rowid via idx_coord_task_runs_task, which is an implementation detail of the query plan - a plan or index change silently stamps the verdict on the wrong attempt.
findings.fix: Add explicit tiebreaks: ORDER BY started_at DESC, rowid DESC and ORDER BY started_at ASC, rowid ASC.

findings.title: idx is not incremented after the team_id WHERE clause
findings.summary: Every other clause in the builder increments idx; the team_id branch does not because it is currently last.
findings.failure_scenario: The next filter appended reuses the same ?N and binds the wrong value. Placeholder count still matches so the query runs - the failure is a silently wrong result set.
findings.fix: Add idx += 1; after the team_id push.

findings.title: UPSERT overwrites created_at, so the column actually means 'last written'
findings.summary: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET created_at = excluded.created_at replaces the original insert time on every rewrite.
findings.failure_scenario: After the first retry rewrites a journal, list_team_journals' ORDER BY j.created_at DESC (line 126) orders by most-recently-edited while the column name, the public TaskExitJournal::created_at field, and the caller all read it as creation time.
findings.fix: Keep the original (created_at = coord_task_journals.created_at) and add a separate updated_at, or rename the field to updated_at throughout.

findings.title: Locking columns bypass add_column_if_missing and can half-apply
findings.summary: locked_by/locked_at use a bespoke prepare(...).is_ok() probe plus a non-transactional two-statement execute_batch, while add_column_if_missing exists six lines below.
findings.failure_scenario: If the second ALTER fails, the table has locked_by without locked_at; the next boot's probe sees has_locked_by == true and never retries, so every locks.rs query fails on the missing column permanently. The probe also swallows every prepare error (corrupt db reads the same as 'column absent').
findings.fix: Replace with two add_column_if_missing calls - each is independently idempotent, so a partial application self-heals on the next boot.

findings.title: Failed legacy migration can leave FK enforcement OFF for the connection's lifetime
findings.summary: The restore path is a single best-effort batch 'ROLLBACK; PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;'; execute_batch aborts at the first failing statement.
findings.failure_scenario: If ROLLBACK errors (no transaction active because the batch failed at BEGIN itself - see B6-01), the PRAGMA never runs and FK enforcement stays OFF. Today the subsequent return Err keeps the store unpublished (coord_stores.rs:66), so the damage is contained by an undocumented coupling.
findings.fix: Split into two independent execute_batch calls so the pragma restore cannot be skipped.

findings.title: acquire_lock is not mutually exclusive against the same agent_id and silently refreshes locked_at
findings.summary: The OR locked_by = ?1 arm makes a second acquire by the same agent succeed and re-stamp locked_at, while the dispatcher documents the call as an atomic claim that 'loses harmlessly to a racing claimer' (schedule/mod.rs:153).
findings.failure_scenario: The double-claim window currently appears closed by dispatcher-side bookkeeping (select_schedulable only sees pending rows; self.running gates re-selection), so this is a contract gap - the safety lives entirely outside the store, in a caller comment asserting the opposite. The locked_at refresh also turns 'how long has this been held' into 'how long since the last acquire attempt', which is exactly what release_stale_locks keys on.
findings.fix: Take the lock only when locked_by IS NULL and return a typed AlreadyHeld(agent_id); add an explicit renew_lock only if a caller needs it (R10). At minimum correct the dispatcher comment.

findings.title: Stale-lock expiry is wall-clock on both sides with no monotonic component
findings.summary: locked_at and the cutoff both come from SystemTime via helpers::now_epoch.
findings.failure_scenario: An NTP step backwards larger than lock_ttl_secs makes every lock look fresh and stale-release stops working; a forward step releases live locks early, producing the superseding-claim scenario documented at select.rs:163-168.
findings.fix: Skip the pass (and warn!) when now_epoch() is less than the maximum locked_at in the table, so a backwards jump degrades to 'no expiry this tick'; document the wall-clock dependency.

verified_clean: No SQL injection: all three format!-built statements interpolate only ?N placeholders and literal column names; schema.rs::add_column_if_missing validates identifiers and all call sites pass literals

Foreign keys enforced: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON set in migrate() on the single long-lived connection (coord.db opened once at agent_init/coord_stores.rs:41), so delete_team_tasks' CASCADE reliance is sound

No lock-ordering or reentrancy hazard from connection_handle(): SqliteSnapshotStore's five methods each acquire and release within one statement; snapshots/operations.rs sequences list_tasks then insert, never nested
Migrations forward-compatible: no DROP outside the guarded one-shot legacy coord_teams rebuild; additive columns via add_column_if_missing; all CREATE are IF NOT EXISTS

Run-row janitor race-free as documented: running-set insert precedes spawn (schedule/mod.rs:178), removal follows finish_task_run (363 -> 484); exactly one globally-unique TeamDispatcher calls abandon_orphaned_runs
GROUP_CONCAT(... ORDER BY ...) requires SQLite >= 3.44 and Cargo.toml:47 pins rusqlite 0.37 with the bundled feature
helpers.rs correct: summarize truncates on chars() (UTF-8 safe, P7); now_epoch uses unwrap_or; db_err total
comments.rs correct: fully parameterised, indexed by (task_id, created_at), no unwrap
Positional row decoding verified column-by-column across all four SELECT sites (row_decode.rs:145, crud.rs:251-253 + indices 14/15/16, deps.rs:45) - all currently agree
cross_cutting: Two separate error policies for corrupt columns (read_task_row fails hard, journal/runs fail soft) chosen per-file rather than per-consequence
helpers::now_epoch is the store's only clock (seconds + wall clock) and is upstream of three findings; SqliteSnapshotStore uses chrono::Utc for the same database - converge on one helper

The derived-status predicate is implemented twice (row_decode::derive_status vs list_tasks' inline SUM(CASE)); the satisfying/dead status sets are string literals in five SQL sites while CoordTaskStatus::satisfies_dependency() exists as an unused single source
delete_team_tasks is the only mutation that emits no topic and no AlephEvent (the caller's notify_team_changed(Deleted) partially compensates)
CoordTaskUpdate's Option<T> fields cannot express 'clear this' - owner and result can never be unset through the store API
Positional row decoding is load-bearing across three hand-written SELECT lists; a shared const TASK_COLUMNS would make drift impossible rather than merely absent
